sources.name: THE unijobs
sources.note: CONTROL PROBE DEGRADED THIS RUN. The mandated invalid-URL probe could not be executed: this run's fetch layer refuses any URL that has not been surfaced by a search engine or by an already-fetched page, so a deliberately fabricated URL cannot be submitted at all. Substituted a DIFFERENTIAL probe that targets the same failure mode (the JREC-IN signature of identical/plausible content returned for distinct requests): fetch several distinct real identifiers on the domain and require that the responses differ from one another and are internally consistent. THE PASSED: the civil-engineering (39 hits), engineering-and-technology (309), mechanical-and-aerospace (64) and other-research-related (144) slugs each returned distinct content, and distinct numeric ids for the same NYUAD job title returned distinct posted/closing dates with correct 'This job has expired' notices rather than byte-identical text. TRAPS CONFIRMED THIS RUN: (1) expired ads stay listed, so status must come from the individual page; (2) the listing cards' relative countdown text is UNRELIABLE - the Adelaide ARC card read '18 days ago' while its own posting page shows a closing date of 7 August 2026, still open. Countdown text was therefore never converted into a deadline; deadlines come only from individual pages. (3) Pagination on this route is a /2/ path suffix, not ?page=2. (4) The engineering-and-technology listing truncates its hrefs to the bare numeric id, and a bare-id URL could not be opened this run, so those rows were DROPPED rather than reconstructed - a real coverage loss of roughly 20 newer NYUAD/SIT/Lingnan postings visible but unreachable.

sources.name: AcademicPositions.com
sources.note: The engineering postdoc feed reports 125 jobs across 5 pages; pages 1-2 and the all-fields post-doc listing were read this run. Listing pages only - individual /ad/ pages were not opened, so department and posted date are never populated. TRAP CONFIRMED: the narrower slugs /field/structural-engineering and /field/engineering-civil-engineering both returned HTTP 403 this run even though search results show them carrying 3 and several postdocs respectively; nothing was taken from them. Substantive finding: across the ~85 engineering and all-fields postdocs read, NOT ONE is structural, civil, earthquake or geotechnical engineering - the feed is dominated by photonics, robotics, quantum, energy chemistry and Mohammed VI Polytechnic life-sciences ads. Many listed deadlines are already in the past, so this feed is not recency-sorted.

sources.name: IIT Kanpur - Civil Engineering
sources.note: Departmental postdoc page. States applications are invited from persons holding a PhD in Civil Engineering or a closely related field, are accepted round the year and given prompt consideration, and are submitted through the Pingala portal. No dated vacancy, no deadline, no stipend figure and no location string are shown, so all are null. Country is null because the page displays no location string - it is deliberately NOT deduced from the institution name.

sources.name: researchersjob.com
sources.note: Front page read this run. The four most recent items are frontier AI (EPFL), pharmacometrics (Uppsala), and two Indian teaching-faculty adverts. ZERO structural, civil, earthquake, geotechnical or mechanical engineering postings. This repeats the previous run's finding and is information, not a fetch failure. The ?s= field searches could not be run this run because the fetch layer would not accept those query URLs without prior provenance.

sources.name: jobs.ac.uk
sources.note: QUARANTINED BY CONTROL PROBE - FAILED. The keyword parameter is not honoured. Seven different queries (structural engineering, civil engineering, finite element, structural dynamics, computational mechanics, earthquake engineering, and the deliberate nonsense string 'zzzqqxnonsenseterm', plus the off-discipline control 'medieval poetry') EACH returned the SAME 16 jobs, all civil/built-environment. A nonsense string and 'medieval poetry' returning 16 civil-engineering postings is the exact confabulation signature this probe exists to catch. Because the discovery layer is unreliable, no posting discovered through it can be trusted to be current or correctly associated, so ZERO records were accepted - including the handful that individually resolved. Note for contrast: individual /job/<ref>/ pages DID return coherent, correctly-expired content when opened directly, so the defect appears to be in the search endpoint rather than in the posting pages. Needs re-checking next run. This is the single largest coverage loss this run: jobs.ac.uk supplied a large share of the previous build.

sources.name: IIT Delhi
sources.note: NOT POLLED THIS RUN. The fetch layer refused the URL for lack of provenance (it accepts only URLs surfaced by a search engine or by an already-fetched page, and this run was unattended so the permission prompt could not be answered). No data carried forward from the previous build, because a stale record presented as current is exactly the hazard this system exists to avoid.

sources.name: IIT Roorkee
sources.note: NOT POLLED THIS RUN. Same provenance refusal as IIT Delhi. Nothing carried forward.

sources.name: IndiaBioscience
sources.note: NOT POLLED THIS RUN (provenance refusal). Life sciences only - it has never carried this field and its absence costs this dataset nothing in-discipline.

sources.name: Indian engineering-postdoc aggregators
sources.note: No Indian aggregator covers engineering postdocs; confirmed over successive runs. FacultyPlus and FacultyTick carry teaching-faculty and administrative posts, not structural/civil postdocs. The realistic route for this field in India is per-institution project-position pages.

sources.name: JREC-IN Portal (Japan)
sources.note: QUARANTINED BY CONTROL PROBE. Requests for three deliberately invalid job IDs each returned complete, plausible postings instead of an error; two were byte-identical. The site executes search via POST with server-side session state and renders rows client-side, so a plain GET returns no listings and the fetch layer confabulated. Zero records accepted. Needs a JS-capable browser fetch. Not re-probed this run - a fabricated URL cannot be submitted through this run's fetch layer.

sources.name: Academic Jobs Online
sources.note: Rows were readable with [POSTDOC] tags and deadlines, but no per-row hyperlink survived the fetch. Records without an individual posting URL are rejected by policy, so all were dropped. Every visible row was also long expired.

sources.name: IIT Delhi IRD vacancies board
sources.note: DEAD DATA. Every row carries a 2017 advertisement number (IITD/IRD/117-125/2017) with deadlines in July-August 2017. Also serves a TLS certificate that does not match its own hostname. Nothing taken from it, deliberately not polled.

sources.name: EURAXESS
sources.note: robots.txt ends with 'Disallow: /jobs/*' and 'Disallow: /*?', closing the search and every detail page plus all pagination. Not polled. This remains the single biggest coverage loss for European structural engineering - the only sanctioned integration is institutions pushing XML in, via support@euraxess.eu.

sources.name: Nature Careers
sources.note: robots.txt disallows /naturecareers/jobs/search and /naturecareers/jobsrss/, and issues 'Disallow: /' for User-Agent anthropic-ai and ClaudeBot by name. Not polled.

sources.name: FindAPostDoc
sources.note: 403 on robots.txt and every listing path. The one route that responds served postings with 2017 deadlines. Rejected as a stale-data hazard.

sources.name: HigherEdJobs
sources.note: Incapsula WAF challenge on both the RSS path and search. Not pollable without dedicated anti-bot handling.

sources.name: ANRF / CSIR / DST (India, government)
sources.note: ANRF renders calls into empty client-side containers. CSIR-HRDG's front door is a language-selection splash and its RA page is a static guidelines document with no announcement stream. DST's announcement list carries no dates at all. Payloads are PDFs. No per-position stream exists to ingest.
